definitions.type: function from natural numbers to real Euclidean spaces
definitions.definition: For each natural k, Rn(k)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), the space of real k-tuples with distance (sum over j<k of |x_j-y_j|^2)^(1/2), with its standard Borel measurable structure. Rn(0) is the one-point space.
I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}, with the usual real metric.

definitions.type: subset of the metric product Rn(n)×ℝ
definitions.definition: Fmax=E×I. The ambient product distance between (x,t) and (y,u) is max(dist(x,y),|t-u|); use the Borel measurable structure.

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure H^a(A) with values in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z, subset C⊆Z and real exponent a≥0, H^a(C) is the unnormalized Hausdorff outer measure with diameter-power cost: supremum over extended scales r>0 of the infimum, over countable covers C⊆⋃_i U_i with extended diameters ediam(U_i)≤r, of Σ_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty}(ediam(U_i))^a. Here ediam is the supremum of pairwise extended distances, with ediam(∅)=0. The inner supremum is zero for an empty member. For a>0 the cost is simply Σ_i(ediam(U_i))^a. No ball-volume or exponent-dependent normalization is included. The notation H^a(C) denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a C in the frozen basis.

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a subset C of an extended metric space Z, dimH C is its Hausdorff dimension: the infimum of positive real exponents a for which H^a(C)=0, embedded in [0,∞], with infimum of the empty set equal to ∞. In particular the empty set has dimension zero. This is the Hausdorff critical exponent convention of the frozen Mathlib dimH. A definition alone does not supply measure-dimension comparison theorems.

For real v, ofReal v is max(v,0) embedded into the extended nonnegative reals. Nonnegative real exponents and the real constant 1 in dimension inequalities are embedded this way. The dimension codomain [0,∞] has its usual extended order and addition.
